findings.trigger_condition: A large valid edge stream contains many unhashable nodes, or repeatedly references unhashable endpoints after many such nodes have been registered (including a duplicate-edge-heavy stream).
findings.root_cause: _id_of performs linear equality scans over unhashable_ids for every lookup and, for an unhashable value, also scans hashable_ids. It has no identity/alias cache for repeated objects. Consequently node registration is quadratic for distinct unhashable nodes and repeated-edge processing can cost O(E*V) equality checks even though seen_edges later discards the duplicates.
findings.impact: Deep acyclic inputs with unhashable nodes can take quadratic time and become effectively non-terminating or CPU-exhausting at practical sizes, undermining the contract's requirement to handle very deep acyclic graphs; deduplication does not protect against a duplicate-edge denial of service because endpoint lookup happens first.
findings.suggested_validation: Use an unhashable node class whose __eq__ increments a counter and compares by identity. Build one-shot chain generators at sizes N and 2N, then add many repeated edges involving a late-registered node. Verify that equality calls/runtime grow approximately fourfold for the chains and by O(V) per duplicate edge; also compare against hashable-node scaling.
